products.name: Chat & research
products.headline: Get from a question to a clearer picture.
products.summary: Work through an idea, investigate a topic or turn a pile of information into a useful brief.
products.description: Start a conversation in Grok, attach the material you want it to inspect and explain the decision you are trying to make. For a current story, ask it to search, open the original sources and attach dates to its findings.
use: Compare competing explanations with source links.
Extract decisions and open questions from a document.
Turn a technical topic into an explanation at your level.
products.boundary: An answer about today needs current sources. A model’s training knowledge alone does not establish what happened today.

products.name: Voice
products.headline: Think out loud. Keep the conversation moving.
products.summary: Use spoken back-and-forth for explanations, rehearsals and hands-free questions.
products.description: A voice conversation is useful when the next question depends on the previous answer. Give it a role, a pace and a stopping point. The consumer voice experience and a developer-built Voice API agent have different setup and billing.
use: Practise an interview one question at a time.
Ask for a slower explanation and challenge the reasoning.
Rehearse a short presentation with targeted feedback.
products.boundary: This guide does not access your microphone. Open Grok to start a real voice session; availability and limits depend on your account.

products.name: Imagine
products.headline: Give the picture a direction.
products.summary: Explore image and video ideas with an intentional subject, composition, light and motion.
products.description: Describe the scene before adding stylistic detail. For an edit, identify what should stay fixed and what should change. Image generation, image editing and video generation use their own tools and models.
use: Develop three visual directions for one idea.
Refine a composition using your own reference material.
Plan a short video shot before generating it.
products.boundary: Review the result at its intended size. Check small text, repeated objects and motion continuity, then refine the specific part that needs work.

products.name: Build
products.headline: Give the coding agent the whole problem.
products.summary: Explore a codebase, investigate a bug and work toward a tested change.
products.description: Grok Build is a coding agent with a terminal workflow. A useful request names the repository, the behavior you expect and how the result will be checked. Ask for an explanation of the existing structure before a broad change.
use: Map an unfamiliar project and its main entry points.
Reproduce a defect and propose a focused fix.
Create a small feature with an explicit acceptance check.
products.boundary: A plausible patch still needs tests and review. This page prepares a brief; it does not connect to or edit your repository.

products.name: Bot
products.headline: A named teammate for a repeatable job.
products.summary: Hand multi-step work to a Bot that keeps its role, context and cloud computer.
products.description: Give one Bot a focused responsibility and the tools it needs. Start with a single useful task, inspect the result, then turn a reliable process into a skill or a routine when recurring work makes sense.
use: Prepare a linked weekly research digest.
Collect evidence for a support investigation.
Draft a recurring report from connected tools.
products.boundary: Account access, consequential actions and scheduled work need deliberate boundaries. Product availability and permissions determine what a Bot can actually do.

products.name: API
products.headline: Build Grok into your own experience.
products.summary: Choose the model, inputs and tools for an application you control.
products.description: The API is the developer interface. Text and image inputs, generated media, speech and search have different model or tool requirements. Compare the dated references below, then verify the current API docs before shipping.
use: Return structured data from a document.
Add a source-aware research workflow to an app.
Connect speech or image generation to your own interface.
products.boundary: API usage is billed separately from consumer subscription allowances. Keep API keys on a server; this page never asks for one.

levels.label: 01 / Introduction
levels.description: Learn the difference between the products and give your first request a useful shape.

levels.name: Get useful results
levels.label: 02 / Beginner
levels.description: Practice research, visual direction and voice with a clear way to judge the result.

levels.name: Work with context
levels.label: 03 / Intermediate

lessons.title: Choose the right starting point
lessons.intro: Begin with the kind of result you want. A conversation, a generated image and a completed task need different interfaces. Choosing that first removes a surprising amount of friction.

steps.title: Name the outcome
steps.text: Write down the thing you want to have at the end: an explanation, a source-linked brief, a visual, a code change or a recurring report.

steps.title: Match the working surface
steps.text: Use chat for a conversation; Imagine for generated media; Build for a coding workflow; Bot for work across tools. Developers can assemble their own experience through the API.

steps.title: Set a finish line
steps.text: Describe how you will judge the result. A five-bullet summary with links is easier to assess than a request to tell you everything.

lessons.check: You can explain which product you chose and what a successful result will look like.
lessons.prompt: Help me choose the right Grok product for this outcome: [describe the result]. Explain the inputs I need, the interface to start with and one concrete way to check the result. Ask about missing context before recommending a workflow.

lessons.title: Write a brief that finishes well
lessons.intro: A strong request makes the goal and the deliverable visible. Add relevant context, practical constraints and an output format, then give the model room to ask about anything that would change the answer.

steps.title: Lead with the job
steps.text: Say what you want done and who the result is for. Include a document, a source link or an example of the quality you expect.

steps.title: Add the boundaries
steps.text: Specify the scope, the date range and any decisions already made. Leave personal details out of a public example.

steps.title: Specify a useful return
steps.text: Ask for the answer in a form you can inspect: a comparison, a draft, a checklist or a proposed change with a validation plan.

lessons.check: Someone reading the request can identify the goal, inputs, constraints and expected output without guessing.
lessons.prompt: Outcome: [what I want to achieve]. Context: [relevant facts or attached material]. Constraints: [scope, time, things to preserve]. Return: [format and length]. Before starting, ask only for missing information that would materially change the result. Label assumptions.

lessons.title: Check the answer before using it
lessons.intro: Treat the first result as something to inspect. A fluent explanation can still mix a fact with an interpretation. Ask the model to make that distinction visible and reopen the material that matters.

steps.title: Check a specific claim
steps.text: Pick the date, number or quote that matters most. Open its linked source and find the passage that supports it.

steps.title: Ask for uncertainty
steps.text: Have the model separate documented facts, its own inference and unresolved questions. Missing evidence should remain visible.

steps.title: Revise the brief
steps.text: If the answer misses the point, name the exact change you need and preserve the parts that worked.

lessons.check: At least one important claim has been traced to its source, with the publication date and scope checked.
lessons.prompt: Audit the answer above. Separate supported facts, interpretations and open questions. For each important factual claim, give its original source and date if available. Identify any statement that the linked material does not actually establish, then revise that statement.

lessons.title: Build a brief from current sources
lessons.intro: A useful research brief answers a decision rather than collecting links. Choose a tight question and a time window, then ask for original announcements, filings or documentation where those exist.

steps.title: Define the question
steps.text: For example, ask what has changed in the last month and how those changes affect a particular owner, developer or reader.

steps.title: Request current evidence
steps.text: In a search-capable experience, ask for source retrieval explicitly. Distinguish the date an event happened from the date an article discussed it.

steps.title: Inspect the synthesis
steps.text: Read the supporting pages for the main conclusion. Keep an announced target separate from a shipped feature or a confirmed delivery.

lessons.check: The brief includes original links, dates, a clear conclusion and a list of gaps worth following up.
lessons.prompt: Research [specific question] for [audience] using current sources within [date range]. Prioritise original announcements and documentation. Return a short conclusion, a table of what changed with event and publication dates, links for key claims and unresolved questions. Distinguish announced plans from available products.

lessons.title: Direct an image or a short scene
lessons.intro: Think like an art director. Subject, composition and lighting give an image a readable structure; a video also needs a deliberate action and camera movement. Start with one clear visual idea.

steps.title: Describe the frame
steps.text: Name the subject, environment, viewpoint and aspect ratio. Explain where the eye should go first.

steps.title: Add one visual direction
steps.text: Choose a lighting mood, material treatment and color palette. Avoid a long list of competing styles.

steps.title: Refine one variable
steps.text: Compare versions by changing a single element. For an edit, state which parts of your reference must remain consistent.

lessons.check: The brief communicates the subject, composition and intended visual treatment before technical effects.
lessons.prompt: Create a visual concept for [subject]. Composition: [viewpoint and focal point]. Setting: [environment]. Lighting: [mood and direction]. Palette: [colors]. Format: [aspect ratio]. Preserve: [important details]. For a video version, use one coherent action and describe a restrained camera movement.

lessons.title: Make voice a useful back-and-forth
lessons.intro: A spoken conversation works best with a role and a rhythm. Choose a short exercise, say how feedback should be delivered and ask for one question at a time so the session stays manageable.

steps.title: Pick the exercise
steps.text: Use a mock interview, language practice or an explanation of an unfamiliar topic. Tell Grok your starting level.

steps.title: Control the pace
steps.text: Ask for short turns and time to answer. Tell it when you want a hint or a simpler explanation.

steps.title: Finish with a review
steps.text: End with a recap of what improved and the next thing to practice. Verify important factual details against a written source.

lessons.check: The conversation has a clear pace, a stopping point and feedback you can act on.
lessons.prompt: Act as my practice partner for [topic or situation]. My starting level is [level]. Ask one short question at a time and wait for my answer. Give specific feedback after each response. After five turns, summarise two strengths and two practical improvements.

lessons.title: Turn a document into a decision aid
lessons.intro: Choose material you are entitled to use and tell Grok what to extract. A decision log, a comparison or a set of unanswered questions is often more useful than a generic summary.

steps.title: Choose the evidence
steps.text: Attach the relevant file or provide the source in a supported interface. Explain whether it is complete and which sections matter.

steps.title: Make extraction traceable
steps.text: Ask for a section, page or cell reference for each key item where the format allows it. Preserve units and dates.

steps.title: Check the difficult parts
steps.text: Inspect footnotes, ambiguous tables and missing pages. Tell it to flag unavailable information instead of inventing a value.

lessons.check: You can trace the extracted decisions and numbers back to the material you supplied.
lessons.prompt: Using the attached document, produce a decision log with columns for decision, supporting passage or page, owner, date and open question. Preserve the source units and wording for important figures. Mark missing information explicitly and do not infer an owner or deadline that is not stated.

lessons.title: Take a bug from symptom to review
lessons.intro: Give a coding agent the observed behavior, the expected behavior and a way to reproduce the gap. A focused brief lets it investigate before changing the project and gives you something concrete to review.

steps.title: Show the failure
steps.text: Supply the error, input and relevant environment. Ask it to identify the entry point and read the existing conventions.

steps.title: Agree on a check
steps.text: Describe a reproducible example or a behavior test. A meaningful test should fail for the reported bug and pass for the intended behavior.

steps.title: Review the resulting change
steps.text: Ask for a concise explanation of the cause, the files changed and the validation result. Inspect assumptions before publishing.

lessons.check: The proposed fix has a reproduction, a focused diff and a recorded validation result.
lessons.prompt: Investigate this defect: [symptom and reproduction]. Expected behavior: [expectation]. Read the relevant code and project instructions first. Explain the likely cause, implement a focused fix and run an appropriate behavior check. Return the changed files, test results and any unresolved limitations. Prepare a reviewable change before publishing.

lessons.title: Create one Bot with a clear job
lessons.intro: Give a Bot a stable responsibility rather than every task at once. Describe the job, the sources it should use and the output you want to receive. Start with a one-time assignment before adding automation.

steps.title: Set up the role
steps.text: Install the official app, sign in and confirm your eligible access. Create a Bot with a short name and one primary responsibility.

steps.title: Connect useful context
steps.text: Use a supported connected app when available, or take over its computer for a necessary sign-in. Keep credentials out of ordinary prompt examples.

steps.title: Inspect the first delivery
steps.text: Choose a small research or drafting task. Ask for links, assumptions and a clear point where further action needs your review.

lessons.check: The Bot has completed one scoped task using the intended sources, and its standing role is understandable.
lessons.prompt: Your role is [focused responsibility]. Use [approved source systems] to prepare [specific deliverable] for [audience]. Preserve source links and identify missing inputs. For this first run, prepare the result in this conversation and wait for review before contacting anyone or publishing changes.

lessons.title: Specify an API workflow before building
lessons.intro: An integration needs more than a model name. Define the input, expected output, tools, failure behavior and budget. Treat latency and task quality as things to measure with your own examples.

steps.title: Choose the interface
steps.text: Identify whether the job needs text, generated media, speech or current search. Check the corresponding model and tool documentation.

steps.title: Define the contract
steps.text: Specify an output schema and how your application handles missing evidence, malformed responses, timeouts and retries.

steps.title: Create an evaluation set
steps.text: Use representative inputs with expected outcomes. Measure quality and cost together, keeping credentials on the server.

lessons.check: The integration has an input/output contract, a small evaluation set and explicit failure behavior.
lessons.prompt: Design an API workflow for [use case]. Specify inputs, output schema, candidate models or tools, server-side credential handling, failure modes, retry rules and a small evaluation dataset. Use current official documentation for availability and pricing. Separate token costs from search, media and other charges.

lessons.title: Save the method that worked
lessons.intro: Once a task reliably produces the right result, turn its method into reusable instructions. Capture why each step exists and how to validate it so the process survives a slightly different input.

steps.title: Capture the sequence
steps.text: List the inputs, source systems and decisions made during the successful run. Keep the result format explicit.

steps.title: Add edge cases
steps.text: Explain what should happen when a source is missing, a value is ambiguous or the expected result is empty.

steps.title: Test a new example
steps.text: Run the saved skill on a different safe input and inspect the result before using it as a recurring process.

lessons.check: A second input produces the intended result without relying on an unstated assumption from the first run.
lessons.prompt: Turn the process we just validated into a reusable skill called [name]. Include when to use it, required inputs and access, the work sequence, decision rules, output format and validation. Add explicit behavior for missing or stale data, and preserve the review boundaries we agreed.

lessons.title: Schedule a routine you can trust
lessons.intro: A routine should make repeated work easier to inspect. Start from a tested skill and choose a clear schedule, input source and place for the result. Decide what happens when the job cannot finish.

steps.title: Define ownership and time
steps.text: Choose the owning Bot, the time zone and the schedule or supported trigger. Make the scope narrow enough to avoid irrelevant runs.

steps.title: Specify success and failure
steps.text: Name the current source, expected output and completion signal. Ask it to report missing input rather than quietly reuse an old result.

steps.title: Run and inspect once
steps.text: Check the first run and the effect of its actions. Revisit the process when a source, website or connected tool changes.

lessons.check: The routine has a clear owner, schedule, current input, output destination and failure message.
lessons.prompt: After we validate [skill name], run it [schedule and time zone] using [current source]. Return [format] in this conversation with the source timestamp and run outcome. If a required source is missing or stale, report that failure and stop. Keep [specific consequential actions] for my review.

templates.name: Research brief
templates.goal: Understand what changed and why it matters
templates.constraints: Use original sources, include dates and distinguish announcements from availability.
templates.format: A short conclusion, a source-linked comparison and open questions.

templates.name: Tesla comparison
templates.goal: Compare two exact Tesla model and trim references
templates.context: Country, model year, trims, driving pattern and home charging access
templates.constraints: Use current local specifications. Keep WLTP and EPA figures distinct. Cite charging conditions and distinguish peak kW from charging time.
templates.format: A comparison table, ownership trade-offs and a practical recommendation with assumptions.

templates.name: Visual direction
templates.goal: Develop a coherent image or short video concept
templates.context: Subject, audience, aspect ratio, setting and reference material
templates.constraints: Keep the subject and composition clear. Specify lighting, palette and what must remain consistent.
templates.format: Three distinct visual directions followed by one refined generation brief.

templates.name: Voice practice
templates.goal: Practice a conversation with useful feedback
templates.constraints: Ask one question at a time, wait for my response and keep turns short.
templates.format: Five practice turns followed by specific strengths and improvements.

templates.name: Coding task
templates.goal: Reproduce and fix a specific software defect
templates.context: Repository, relevant files, observed behavior and expected behavior
templates.constraints: Read project conventions, keep the change focused and run a meaningful validation.
templates.format: A reviewable change with the cause, changed files, checks and limitations.

templates.name: Weekly Bot
templates.goal: Prepare a recurring source-linked research digest
templates.context: Topic, approved sources, audience, schedule and time zone
templates.constraints: Validate one run before scheduling. Report missing or stale inputs. Prepare drafts for review before sending or publishing.
templates.format: Five developments, why each matters, original links and questions to follow.

templates.name: API project
templates.goal: Design a useful AI feature with a measurable result
templates.context: Users, input format, output contract, tools and budget
templates.constraints: Keep keys server-side. Define validation, retries and failure behavior. Use current model and pricing documentation.
templates.format: An implementation plan, output schema, evaluation set and cost assumptions.

templates.name: Document review
templates.goal: Extract decisions and unresolved questions from a document
templates.context: The attached document, its date and the decision I need to make
templates.constraints: Preserve units and dates. Cite pages or sections. Mark missing information and separate inference from source facts.
templates.format: A concise summary, decision log and questions for follow-up.
